goal: Learn Kubernetes deeply and pass the CKA exam, including hands-on cluster setup
interpretation: In 45 minutes of viewing, the learner gets a solid conceptual foundation in Kubernetes architecture, core objects, kubectl, and kubeadm cluster setup, framed around the CKA exam, along with a clear picture of the exam's scope and what to study next.
assumptions: 'Nothing from before 2023' means videos must be published in 2023 or later, and since titles are the only signal available, titles that mention older years or outdated exam versions are excluded.
The learner will use the remaining CKA preparation (practice labs, mock exams) outside this 45-minute video plan.
The learner has no prior Kubernetes exposure, so the plan starts at architecture and does not assume cloud-managed clusters.
The current CKA curriculum covers cluster architecture/installation/configuration, workloads and scheduling, services and networking, storage, and troubleshooting.
feasibility_note: Deep Kubernetes mastery and passing the CKA cannot be achieved in 45 minutes of video. Realistic in this budget: understand the CKA scope and format, learn Kubernetes architecture, pods/deployments/services, core kubectl usage, and see a kubeadm cluster setup walkthrough, which gives a foundation for later hands-on practice and mock exams.

sub_topics.title: CKA exam format, domains and study strategy
sub_topics.why: The learner needs exam-prep orientation: what the current CKA covers, the weighting of domains, and the time-pressured, hands-on format.

sub_topics.title: Kubernetes architecture: control plane and worker node components
sub_topics.why: Coming from single-server Docker, the learner must understand how API server, etcd, scheduler, controller manager, kubelet and kube-proxy fit together to orchestrate containers across nodes.

sub_topics.title: Pods, ReplicaSets and Deployments
sub_topics.why: These are the core workload objects replacing 'docker run'; the learner knows containers but not how Kubernetes schedules, scales and updates them declaratively with YAML.

sub_topics.title: Services and basic cluster networking
sub_topics.why: Single-server Docker port mapping differs from Kubernetes Services (ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer) and DNS, which are heavily tested in the CKA.

sub_topics.title: kubectl essentials and exam-speed imperative commands
sub_topics.why: The CKA is a command-line practical exam; the learner needs fast kubectl usage, imperative commands, dry-run YAML generation, and kubectl explain/docs navigation.

sub_topics.title: Cluster setup with kubeadm
sub_topics.why: Hands-on cluster installation (init, join, CNI, node prep) is a core CKA domain and the learner has never built a multi-node cluster.

picks.title: CKA Exam Prep: How I Became a Kubestronaut
picks.reason: Gives a CKA-specific roadmap of exam format and key topics, and it is the only post-2023 exam-overview video that fits the 4-minute slot. This sets the scope before any Kubernetes content.
picks.confidence_note: The transcript is unavailable, so the content is judged from the title and summary only. Confidence would rise if the video shows the current exam domains and weightings.

picks.title: Kubernetes Architecture Explained: Control Plane, Nodes & Pod Lifecycle | CKA Ch 1.1
picks.reason: A CKA-chapter video that covers control plane components (kube-apiserver, etcd, scheduler, controller-manager) and node components (kubelet, runtime, kube-proxy, CNI). It also walks the Deployment-to-Running-Pod lifecycle and shows how to match failure symptoms to components, which is useful for troubleshooting questions.
picks.confidence_note: The summary matches the slot well and is exam-oriented. There is no transcript or verified quote, and the segment map looks incomplete.

picks.title: EP05 - Kubernetes Deployments & ReplicaSets
picks.reason: Explains Deployments and ReplicaSets (self-healing, scaling, rolling updates), then creates a Deployment from a YAML manifest with kubectl. This gives a Docker user the jump from single containers to managed replicas.
picks.confidence_note: Short and hands-on, but it is not CKA-framed and has no transcript. Pods on their own are covered only lightly.

picks.title: Stop Losing Easy Points on the CKA: Complete NodePort Workflow (CKA Trap)
picks.reason: A CKA-oriented NodePort workflow that exposes a Deployment. It covers common exam traps: missing container ports, invalid kubectl flags, and selector mismatches that leave a Service with no Endpoints.
picks.confidence_note: Strong on exam practice but narrow, since it covers NodePort only. ClusterIP and LoadBalancer concepts are not clearly covered, and it has no transcript.

picks.title: Day 13: Imperative commands for Deployments, Services and Troubleshooting | CKA Course 2025
picks.reason: Part of a CKA 2025 course on imperative commands for Deployments, Services and troubleshooting, which is the exam-speed kubectl skill needed. Only the opening segment is used to fit the budget.
picks.confidence_note: The card has no internal segment map, so the 0-9 minute range is an assumption. Confidence would rise if the opening minutes are confirmed to cover core imperative commands.

picks.title: How to Install Kubernetes with Kubeadm (2025 Update) | Full Cluster Setup Walkthrough
picks.reason: A step-by-step kubeadm cluster install on Ubuntu 22.04 with containerd and Calico CNI. It has no red flags and was updated for 2025, so the learner sees the init and join flow that the CKA tests.
picks.confidence_note: This is the only unflagged, recent, short kubeadm walkthrough. The segment map covers only 4:30 of a 9.1-minute video, and there is no transcript.

warnings: Feasibility: deep Kubernetes mastery and passing the CKA cannot be achieved in 45 minutes of video. This plan is a foundation only; the CKA is a hands-on exam, so you need lab practice and mock exams afterwards.

No verified quotes were available for any candidate, and every transcript is poor or metadata-only. Every pick is therefore judged from titles and summaries and carries moderate confidence; evidence_quote_ids are empty throughout.
The kubectl pick uses an assumed 0-9 minute range of a 31-minute lecture, because the card has no segment map. Check that the range makes sense and keep watching if it is useful.
Services coverage is thin: the pick covers NodePort and the endpoints/selector workflow, but ClusterIP, LoadBalancer and basic cluster networking concepts get little time.
Pods get light direct coverage, because the pick focuses on Deployments and ReplicaSets.
Coverage of CKA domains is partial. Storage, scheduling details, RBAC, etcd backup and troubleshooting are not covered and need separate study.
The kubeadm video's segment map covers only part of its 9.1 minutes. The whole video is counted toward the budget.
Planned viewing is 42.7 of 45 minutes (about 95%). The 2.3 unused minutes are left because no fitting, unflagged, post-2023 video was available to add.
All picks come from 2023 or later, using upload dates as the check. Titles that mention future years were not trusted over the metadata.
